findings: The manual tenant-ID fallback is not covered; the integration flow always requires a tenant combobox.
The mock fixture always returns a nonempty tenant list, so the manual tenant-ID form and confirmation behavior are untested.
Live integration tests provision a unique app registration, service principal, federated credentials, and Reader RBAC assignment per run but define no cleanup; afterEach only writes coverage.

The combined run exposed a flaky desktop auto-save-error case and an interrupted mobile auto-save-error case while snapshotting; the run ended with 10 passed, 1 flaky, 1 interrupted, and 28 did not run.
The roleAssignments mock accepts any PUT and then reports Reader on GET without validating role definition or scope, so an incorrect RBAC request can pass.
No mock seeds different AZURE_CLIENT_ID and AZURE_PLAN_CLIENT_ID values or renders the signed-in card without subscriptionId, leaving the drift warning and subscription guidance unverified.
The live flow accepts either a subscription selector or a no-access message instead of deterministically exercising the no-access and subscription-load-error states.
The test named Selecting an existing repository with environment variables already saved creates a new repository through prepareMockAzureSubscription rather than selecting an existing repository.
No Playwright integration test exists for build, deploy, version comparison, or deployment error states.
No Playwright mock test exists; build success/deploy failure, version mismatch, loading, and network-error UI states are unverified.
No dedicated Playwright integration test exists for refresh, save, revert, callback completion, or key-level validation errors.
The component is exercised only indirectly through parent cards; auto-save results, concurrent refresh/save, and callback behavior are not independently verified.

The fresh-provision path asserts `State container:` immediately after `run()`, but CoreInfraCard keeps its progress rows visible after success and renders the resource inventory only when `steps.length === 0`; as written, this path fails before the later Start over reset. Assert successful step statuses, then reset before checking the inventory.

The provisioning assertions check only that five step labels exist, although all ten rows are initialized before the run, and they do not assert successful terminal statuses. Assert that every step is done or skipped and none is error/running.
No deterministic scenario verifies recovery when the resource group exists but the expected Terraform container is absent, or when the selected subscription drifts after infrastructure exists.
The mock spec does not isolate the resource-group-without-Terraform-container recovery state, leaving the remediation path unverified.

The only mock scenario stops at unmet prerequisites, leaving the ready, provisioning, and error states untested. No V8 coverage artifacts were present to compare; add deterministic mocked scenarios for these branches to improve coverage.
Only a live integration spec exists; pre-verified domains, existing-but-unverified DNS records, and rerun/cleanup behavior are not isolated or deterministically covered.
No mock Playwright test exists, so domain verification and assignment UI behavior cannot be exercised independently of live Azure/DNS dependencies.
No Playwright integration test exists for branch-source selection, disabled creation, protected-branch display, or create errors.
No Playwright mock test exists for the branch creation control and its error state.
No dedicated Playwright integration test isolates environment loading, empty environments, PR locking, branch mismatch warnings, or refresh failures.
Indirect RepoCard coverage does not deterministically assert the locked-by-PR and multiple/no matching branch states.
OAuth initiation/completion, successful PAT submission, and logout are not exercised; the authenticated flow restores state before asserting the signed-in UI.
The mock flow does not submit a valid PAT or exercise logout/token refresh, leaving those user-visible states unverified.
No Playwright integration test exists for terminal relay creation, step failures, rerun behavior, or resource-link rendering.
No Playwright mock test exists for collapse/expand persistence, auto-save after creation, or connection-detail population.
No dedicated Playwright integration test exists for the card-level composition of repository selection and environment locking.
RepoCard is covered only indirectly through RepoDetail tests; the lockedByPR handoff and card-level conditional rendering are not asserted directly.
The fixed-name repository scenario is not rerunnable when the repository already exists, and the clone-environment warning is not forced by the live flow.
The mock suite does not force the clone-environment warning response or stale repository-list/account-switch behavior.
No Playwright integration test exists for all setup-step statuses or progress rendering.
No dedicated mock test verifies done, skipped, error, running, pending, detail, or determinate progress states.
